  "narrative_text": "Four complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: coordinated disruption of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism axis. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068) and its KEGG equivalent (KEGG:map00150) as the top hits with FDR 5.7e-15, driven by five input steroids (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, DHEA, testosterone, and estradiol). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific OSEA confirmed C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00140) as the sole significant hit (p=8.4e-06), with the same five driver compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis independently recovered the androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism network as its top-ranked pathway (p=8.4e-05), also mapping all five steroids plus hydroxysteroid intermediates (5α-androstane-3,17-dione, androsterone) onto the C21-steroid hormone network. Notably, butanone and sulindac did not map to any pathway across all three paradigms, indicating they are treatment-specific or off-target signals unconnected to the steroidogenic axis. The convergent evidence from ORA (enrichment statistics), network-activity (m/z propagation), and multiple databases (SMPDB, KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome) establishes robust, cross-validated perturbation of steroidogenesis in the treatment group. The simultaneous elevation of upstream precursors (DHEA, androstenedione) and downstream effectors (testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estradiol) suggests either enhanced steroidogenic flux or blockade of a terminal conversion step — a pattern consistent with aromatase or 17β-HSD modulation. react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: coordinated disruption of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism axis. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068) and its KEGG equivalent (KEGG:map00150) as the top hits with FDR 5.7e-15, driven by five input steroids (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, DHEA, testosterone, and estradiol). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific OSEA confirmed C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00140) as the sole significant hit (p=8.4e-06), with the same five driver compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis independently recovered the androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism network as its top-ranked pathway (p=8.4e-05), also mapping all five steroids plus hydroxysteroid intermediates (5α-androstane-3,17-dione, androsterone) onto the C21-steroid hormone network. Notably, butanone and sulindac did not map to any pathway across all three paradigms, indicating they are treatment-specific or off-target signals unconnected to the steroidogenic axis. The convergent evidence from ORA (enrichment statistics), network-activity (m/z propagation), and multiple databases (SMPDB, KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome) establishes robust, cross-validated perturbation of steroidogenesis in the treatment group. The simultaneous elevation of upstream precursors (DHEA, androstenedione) and downstream effectors (testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estradiol) suggests either enhanced steroidogenic flux or blockade of a terminal conversion step — a pattern consistent with aromatase or 17β-HSD modulation. This signature is mechanistically linked to cancer proliferation pathways (WP:WP2263, WP:WP5434) and RUNX2-regulated osteoblast programs (REACT:R-HSA-8940973) as downstream biological consequences.

final_claims.claim_text: Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently identifies "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as its top-ranked pathway with p-value 8.4e-05.
Mummichog ranks "C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism" (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as its second pathway with p-value 8.4e-05.
The driver compound 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone) is a member of SMPDB:SMP00068.
The driver compound androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (androstenedione) is a member of SMPDB:SMP00068.
The driver compound dehydroepiandrosterone is a member of SMPDB:SMP00068.
The driver compound testosterone is a member of SMPDB:SMP00068.
The driver compound 17β-estradiol (estradiol) is a member of SMPDB:SMP00068.
Androstenedione (KEGG:C00280) acts as a substrate in the mummichog pathway MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism.
Testosterone (KEGG:C00535) is a product in the mummichog pathway MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism.

Dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) is a driver metabolite of the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism pathway (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism), together with androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and estradiol.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment analysis of seven metabolites using RaMP multi-DB ORA and mummichog m/z-direct activity reveals a convergent signal around steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP ORA identifies the SMPDB pathway "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" (SMPDB:SMP00068) as its top-ranked hit with FDR 5.7e-15, driven by five input steroids that fully overlap with those recovered by mummichog as its top-ranked "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.4e-05, 11/11 input metabolites mapped). The second-highest mummichog pathway, "C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism" (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.4e-05, 12/12 input metabolites mapped), shares the same five driver steroids and maps to the same biological axis. These five driver compounds are dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and estradiol. The remaining two input metabolites, butanone and sulindac, did not map to either recovered pathway in either paradigm.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms converged on a single dominant signal. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068, KEGG:map00150) at rank 2 with FDR 5.74e-15, mapping five androgen and estrogen intermediates: 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone, KEGG:C03917), androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (androstenedione, KEGG:C00280), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), testosterone (KEGG:C00535) and 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovered KEGG:hsa00140 as its sole significant hit at p 8.391e-06 with the identical five-steroid set. Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) first at p 8.4027e-05, hitting 11 compounds including the same five driver steroids plus several hydroxysteroid derivatives. Butanone (KEGG:C02845) and Sulindac (KEGG:C01531) did not map to steroid pathways in any tool, confirming selectivity of the signal. The five driver steroids are coherent substrate and product intermediates in the classical steroidogenesis cascade, centred on the C19/C18 androgen and estrogen hub. Cross-paradigm consensus on a single pathway family with a shared driver set establishes a robust biological interpretation for the treatment effect.
